question.text: Let $P$ and $Q$ be the points on the parabola $y^{2}=4 x$ so that the line segment $P Q$ subtends right angle at the vertex. If $P Q$ intersects the axis of the parabola at $R,$ then the distance of the vertex from $R$ is

solution.text: According to question, it is given that slope of $P X$ and $Q X$ are perpendicular to each other, i.e., slope of $P X \times$ slope of $X Q=-1$ $\Rightarrow \quad \frac{2 t}{t^{2}} \times \frac{2 m}{m^{2}}=-1$ $\Rightarrow \quad t_{m}=-4$ $P Q: \frac{x-t^{2}}{t^{2}-m^{2}}=\frac{y-2 t}{2 t-2 m}$ Let $P Q$ meets axis of parabola i.e, $x$ -axis at $R(\alpha, 0),$ then $\frac{\alpha-t^{2}}{(t+m)(t-m)}=\frac{0-2 t}{2(t-m)}$ $\Rightarrow \quad \alpha-t^{2}=-t^{2}-t m=-t^{2}+4$ $\Rightarrow \quad \alpha=4 \Rightarrow A R=4$
